sections.subtopic: Foundations of Integration: Indefinite Integrals & Standard Forms
sections.title: Integration: undoing the derivative

board_events.text: Integration: undoing the derivative
Differentiation gives a rate of change. Integration reverses it: from the rate, rebuild the function.
If $F'(x)=f(x)$, then $F(x)$ is an anti-derivative of $f(x)$.
Differentiation erases constants, so we can't recover which one — we add $+C$.
The answer is never one curve but a whole family $F(x)+C$, stacked vertically.

board_events.text: Along a line $x=a$, every curve has slope $f(a)$ — shifting up or down never changes steepness.

segments.text: <curious>Let me start with a question that turns everything you know about derivatives around.
Differentiation takes a function and hands you its rate of change. Integration asks the reverse, harder question: given the rate at every instant, can I rebuild the original function?
We name that rebuilt function. If capital F differentiates to little f, then capital F is an anti-derivative of f — it literally un-does the derivative.

Now the crucial catch. When you differentiate, every constant vanishes: x squared plus seven and x squared minus a hundred have the same derivative. Running it backwards, you can't tell which constant was there, so we honestly write plus C.
So the integral of two x is x squared plus C, where C is any constant at all.
That means an indefinite integral is never a single curve. It's an entire family, F of x, F of x plus one, F of x plus two, stacked like a ladder.
Picture that ladder: identical curves, each lifted by its own value of C.

<chuckle>And here's the pretty part. Pick any vertical line x equals a. It cuts every curve, and the tangent at each crossing has the same slope, because sliding a curve up or down never changes how steep it is.
<curious>चलो एक ऐसे सवाल से शुरू करते हैं जो derivatives के बारे में आपकी सोच पलट देगा।
Differentiation किसी function को लेकर उसका rate of change देता है। Integration ठीक उल्टा, मुश्किल सवाल पूछता है: हर instant का rate पता हो, तो क्या original function वापस बन सकता है?
उस वापस बनी function को हम नाम देते हैं। अगर capital F differentiate होकर little f देता है, तो capital F, f का anti-derivative है, यह सचमुच derivative को un-do करता है।

अब असली catch। जब आप differentiate करते हैं, हर constant गायब हो जाता है: x square plus seven और x square minus hundred का derivative same होता है। उल्टा चलने पर पता नहीं चलता कौन सा constant था, इसलिए हम ईमानदारी से plus C लिखते हैं।
तो two x का integral है x square plus C, जहाँ C कोई भी constant हो सकता है।
मतलब indefinite integral कभी एक अकेली curve नहीं होती। यह पूरा family है, F of x, F of x plus one, F of x plus two, ladder की तरह stacked।
उस ladder को देखो: एक जैसी curves, हर एक अपने C के हिसाब से ऊपर उठी हुई।

<chuckle>और यह रहा खूबसूरत हिस्सा। कोई भी vertical line लो, x equals a। यह हर curve को काटती है, और हर crossing पर tangent का slope same रहता है, क्योंकि curve को ऊपर-नीचे खिसकाने से steepness नहीं बदलती।

sections.subtopic: Foundations of Integration: Indefinite Integrals & Standard Forms
sections.title: The standard integral table and linearity

board_events.text: Standard forms and the two workhorse rules

board_events.latex: \int e^x\,dx = e^x + C \qquad \int a^x\,dx = \frac{a^x}{\ln a} + C
\int \cos x\,dx = \sin x + C \qquad \int \sin x\,dx = -\cos x + C
\int \sec^2 x\,dx = \tan x + C \qquad \int \csc^2 x\,dx = -\cot x + C

board_events.text: Linearity: $\int[k_1 f + k_2 g]\,dx = k_1\int f\,dx + k_2\int g\,dx$ — sums and constants only.
Self-check any row by differentiating the right side; if you don't get the integrand back, it's wrong.

segments.text: Here's the toolkit you must know cold. Every direct integral in this subtopic is just pattern-matching to one of these rows.
The power rule: x to the n integrates to x to the n plus one, over n plus one, valid for every n except minus one, where the denominator would blow up.
That single exception, one over x, integrates to log of the absolute value of x. Keep the modulus, since one over x is defined for negative x too.
Exponentials: e to the x integrates to itself; a general base a to the x picks up a division by natural log a.
The trig pair to burn in: cosine integrates to plus sine, but sine integrates to minus cosine. The minus lives with the sine integral.
Secant squared gives tangent; cosecant squared gives minus cotangent, these are just the derivative table read backwards.
And two inverse-trig forms: one over one plus x squared gives arctan x; one over root one minus x squared gives arcsin x.
Tying it together is linearity: you may split sums and pull out constant multiples freely. But never products or quotients, those need real methods later.
One habit makes the whole table self-verifying: differentiate your answer. If it doesn't return the integrand, hunt for the slip.
यह रहा वो toolkit जो रट लेना ज़रूरी है। इस subtopic का हर direct integral बस इन्हीं rows में से किसी से pattern-match करना है।
Power rule: x to the n integrate होकर बनता है x to the n plus one, बटा n plus one, हर n के लिए valid, सिवाय minus one के, जहाँ denominator zero हो जाता।
वही एक exception, one over x, integrate होकर बनता है log of the absolute value of x. Modulus रखना, क्योंकि one over x negative x के लिए भी defined है।
Exponentials: e to the x खुद में integrate होता है; general base a to the x में natural log a का division आ जाता है।
याद रखने वाली trig जोड़ी: cosine integrate होकर plus sine, पर sine integrate होकर minus cosine। Minus हमेशा sine के integral के साथ रहता है।
Secant square देता है tangent; cosecant square देता है minus cotangent, ये बस derivative table को उल्टा पढ़ना है।
और दो inverse-trig forms: one over one plus x square देता है arctan x; one over root one minus x square देता है arcsin x।
इन सबको जोड़ता है linearity: sums को split और constant multiples को बाहर निकाल सकते हैं। पर products या quotients कभी नहीं, उनके लिए आगे अलग methods हैं।
एक आदत पूरी table को self-verifying बना देती है: अपना answer differentiate करो। अगर integrand वापस नहीं मिला, तो गलती ढूँढो।

sections.subtopic: Foundations of Integration: Indefinite Integrals & Standard Forms
sections.title: Worked examples: split, simplify, integrate

board_events.text: Example 1: split with linearity
Evaluate $\int\left(3x^2+\tfrac{4}{x}-5\sec^2 x\right)dx$.
Split term by term, pull out constants, then use rows one, two and seven.
Example 2: divide before you integrate
Evaluate $\int \frac{x^2+2x+5}{x}\,dx$ — the trap is reaching for a substitution.
Split the fraction first: $\frac{x^2+2x+5}{x} = x + 2 + \frac{5}{x}$.
Polynomial over a single monomial? Divide through first — save a minute, skip the substitution.

segments.text: Let's put the table to work. First a clean Board-level split.
We want the integral of three x squared, plus four over x, minus five secant squared x.
Linearity lets us break this into three separate integrals and pull the constants out front, then match rows one, two, and seven of the table.
Row one turns three x squared into x cubed; four over x becomes four log mod x; five secant squared becomes five tan x. Notice the single C at the end, and the modulus inside the log.
<curious>Now a J E E speed trap, where the obvious move is the wrong one.
We want the integral of x squared plus two x plus five, all over x. The trap is reaching for a substitution.
Don't. Just split the fraction term by term: it becomes x plus two plus five over x.
Now every piece is a standard form: x squared over two, plus two x, plus five log mod x, plus C.
The lesson: whenever a polynomial sits over a single monomial, divide through first. You'll save time and dodge a needless substitution.
अब table को काम पर लगाते हैं। पहले एक साफ़ Board-level split।
हमें integral चाहिए three x square, plus four over x, minus five secant square x का।
Linearity से इसे तीन अलग integrals में तोड़ते हैं और constants बाहर निकालते हैं, फिर table की rows one, two, और seven से match करते हैं।
Row one से three x square बनता है x cube; four over x बनता है four log mod x; five secant square बनता है five tan x. ध्यान दो, अंत में एक ही C, और log के अंदर modulus।
<curious>अब एक J E E speed trap, जहाँ obvious move ही गलत है।
हमें integral चाहिए x square plus two x plus five, बटा x का। Trap है substitution की तरफ़ भागना।
मत भागो। बस fraction को term by term split करो: यह बन जाता है x plus two plus five over x।
अब हर piece एक standard form है: x square बटा two, plus two x, plus five log mod x, plus C।
सबक: जब भी polynomial किसी single monomial के ऊपर हो, पहले divide कर दो। समय बचेगा और बेकार का substitution टलेगा।

sections.subtopic: Foundations of Integration: Indefinite Integrals & Standard Forms
sections.title: Worked examples: identities and recovering a function

board_events.text: Example 3: an identity clears the way
Evaluate $\int \frac{\cos 2x}{\cos^2 x\,\sin^2 x}\,dx$.
Use $\cos 2x = \cos^2 x - \sin^2 x$, then split over the denominator.

board_events.latex: \frac{\cos^2 x - \sin^2 x}{\cos^2 x\,\sin^2 x} = \frac{1}{\sin^2 x} - \frac{1}{\cos^2 x} = \csc^2 x - \sec^2 x

board_events.text: Example 4: recover a function from its slope
Given $f'(x)=\frac{(x+1)(x-1)}{x}$ for $x>0$, through $(1,\tfrac{3}{2})$. Simplify: $f'(x)=x-\tfrac{1}{x}$.
The point pins $C$: $\tfrac{3}{2} = \tfrac{1}{2} + C \Rightarrow C = 1$, so $f(x)=\tfrac{x^2}{2}-\ln x + 1$ and $f(e)=\tfrac{e^2}{2}$.
A boundary condition turns the whole family into one function — the bridge to differential equations.

segments.text: This one looks brutal until an identity dissolves it.
We want the integral of cosine two x, over cosine squared x times sine squared x.
Rewrite cosine two x as cosine squared minus sine squared, then split that over the denominator.
The cosine squared over cosine squared sine squared collapses to one over sine squared; the other term to one over cosine squared. Those are cosecant squared minus secant squared.
And those integrate straight from the table: minus cotangent x, minus tangent x, plus C. The whole difficulty was algebraic.
<curious>Now an Advanced problem that hides integration inside a slope question.
We're given f prime of x, and told the graph passes through the point one, three-halves. First simplify the derivative to x minus one over x.
Integrate to get the family: x squared over two, minus log x, plus C.

The passing-through point fixes C. Plug in: three-halves equals one-half plus C, so C is one. That selects one curve, f of x is x squared over two minus log x plus one, and f of e is e squared over two.
The deep idea: a single boundary condition converts an entire family into one unique function. That's exactly the bridge to differential equations later this year.
यह देखने में भयानक लगता है, जब तक एक identity इसे घोल न दे।
हमें integral चाहिए cosine two x, बटा cosine square x times sine square x का।
Cosine two x को लिखो cosine square minus sine square, फिर उसे denominator पर split करो।
Cosine square बटा cosine square sine square सिमटकर one over sine square बनता है; दूसरा term one over cosine square. ये हैं cosecant square minus secant square।
और ये सीधे table से integrate होते हैं: minus cotangent x, minus tangent x, plus C. पूरी मुश्किल बस algebraic थी।
<curious>अब एक Advanced problem जो integration को slope के सवाल में छिपा देती है।
हमें f prime of x दिया है, और बताया है कि graph point one, three-halves से गुज़रता है। पहले derivative को simplify करो x minus one over x।
Integrate करके family निकालो: x square बटा two, minus log x, plus C।
गुज़रने वाला point C को fix करता है। रखो: three-halves बराबर one-half plus C, तो C है one. यह एक curve चुन लेता है, f of x है x square बटा two minus log x plus one, और f of e है e square बटा two।
गहरी बात: एक अकेली boundary condition पूरे family को एक unique function में बदल देती है। यही आगे differential equations का bridge है।

sections.subtopic: Foundations of Integration: Indefinite Integrals & Standard Forms
sections.title: Pitfalls: the +C reflex and forbidden moves

board_events.text: The five slips that cost easy marks
Forgetting $+C$ is the most-penalised Board error. Write it the instant you finish.
Never apply the power rule at $n=-1$: $\int\frac{1}{x}\,dx = \ln|x|+C$, a separate memorised result — not $\frac{x^0}{0}$.
Keep the modulus in $\ln|x|$: the integrand $\frac{1}{x}$ is defined for negative $x$ too, so it's required, not decoration.
Sign trap: $\int \sin x\,dx = -\cos x$ but $\int \cos x\,dx = +\sin x$. The minus lives with sine.
Linearity covers sums and constant multiples only — never $\int(f\cdot g)=\int f\cdot\int g$. Products and quotients need their own methods.
The universal safety net: differentiate your answer. Integration is the one operation you can instantly self-check.

segments.text: Let's lock in the mistakes that quietly bleed marks, because avoiding them is free points.
Number one: forgetting plus C. In Boards it's the most penalised error, a perfect function part still loses marks without it. Train the reflex to write plus C the instant you finish.
Number two: never apply the power rule at n equals minus one. One over x does not become x to the zero over zero. It's a separate, memorised result, log mod x plus C.
Number three: keep the modulus in log mod x. Since one over x is defined for negative x as well, the absolute value is mathematically required, not decoration.
Number four, the classic sign slip: sine integrates to minus cosine, but cosine integrates to plus sine. The minus lives with the sine integral.
Number five: linearity is only for sums and constant multiples. The integral of a product is not the product of integrals, those need their own methods.
<whisper>Here's the secret weapon on the board: differentiate what you wrote, and check it equals the integrand.
Do that every time. Integration is the only school-level operation you can instantly reverse-check, and if the derivative isn't the integrand, you've caught your mistake before the examiner did.
अब उन गलतियों को पक्का कर लें जो चुपचाप marks खा जाती हैं, क्योंकि इन्हें टालना मुफ़्त के points हैं।
पहली: plus C भूलना। Boards में यह सबसे ज़्यादा penalise होने वाली गलती है, perfect function part भी इसके बिना marks खोता है। आदत डालो कि खत्म करते ही plus C लिख दो।
दूसरी: power rule को n equals minus one पर कभी मत लगाओ। One over x कभी x to the zero over zero नहीं बनता। यह अलग, रटा हुआ result है, log mod x plus C।
तीसरी: log mod x में modulus रखो। चूँकि one over x negative x के लिए भी defined है, absolute value mathematically ज़रूरी है, decoration नहीं।
चौथी, classic sign slip: sine integrate होकर minus cosine, पर cosine integrate होकर plus sine. Minus हमेशा sine के integral के साथ।
पाँचवी: linearity सिर्फ़ sums और constant multiples के लिए है। किसी product का integral, integrals का product नहीं होता, उनके अपने methods हैं।
<whisper>यह रहा board पर लिखा secret weapon: जो लिखा उसे differentiate करो, और check करो कि वह integrand के बराबर है।
हर बार यही करो। Integration ही एकमात्र school-level operation है जिसे तुरंत reverse-check कर सकते हैं, और अगर derivative integrand नहीं है, तो examiner से पहले गलती पकड़ ली।

sections.title: Substitution: the chain rule in reverse

board_events.text: Substitution: the chain rule in reverse
The table can't touch $\int 2x\cos(x^2)\,dx$ — there's no entry for $\cos(x^2)$.
Chain rule: $\frac{d}{dx}F(g(x)) = F'(g(x))\,g'(x)$. So (function of $g$)$\times g'$ is a disguised derivative.
The step $du = g'(x)\,dx$ is the exchange rate — forget it and the answer is wrong.

board_events.text: Substitution only helps when $g'(x)$ — or a constant times it — is actually present.
For an indefinite integral, always convert back to $x$ at the end.

segments.text: <curious>What do you do when the integrand simply isn't in the table?
Take the integral of two x times cosine of x squared. There's no row for cosine of x squared, so we're stuck, until we reshape it.

The idea mirrors the chain rule in reverse. The chain rule says the derivative of F of g of x is F prime of g, times g prime of x. So if an integrand looks like a function of g, times g prime, it's exactly a disguised derivative.
So we peel off the inner function, call it u, and the whole thing becomes the integral of f of u, du, clean and familiar.
The one step everyone forgets is the accounting: d u equals g prime of x d x. Think of it as the exchange rate, drop it and your answer is off by a factor.
Picture converting rupees to another currency: switch to the u-world, do the easy shopping, then convert your answer back to the x-world.
Substitution only helps when g prime of x, or a constant multiple of it, is actually sitting in the integrand. If it's missing, this method stalls.
And for an indefinite integral, always convert back to x at the very end, never leave your answer in u.
<curious>क्या करोगे जब integrand table में है ही नहीं?
लो integral two x times cosine of x square का। Cosine of x square की कोई row नहीं, तो हम अटक गए, जब तक इसे reshape न करें।

Idea chain rule का उल्टा है। Chain rule कहता है F of g of x का derivative है F prime of g, times g prime of x. तो अगर integrand दिखे function of g, times g prime जैसा, तो यह बिलकुल एक छिपा हुआ derivative है।
तो हम inner function छील लेते हैं, उसे u कहते हैं, और पूरी चीज़ बन जाती है integral of f of u, du, साफ़ और जाना-पहचाना।
एक step जो सब भूलते हैं वो है accounting: d u बराबर g prime of x d x. इसे exchange rate समझो, छोड़ा तो answer factor भर गलत हो जाएगा।
सोचो rupees को दूसरी currency में बदलना: u-world में जाओ, आसान shopping करो, फिर answer वापस x-world में बदलो।
Substitution तभी काम आता है जब g prime of x, या उसका constant multiple, सचमुच integrand में मौजूद हो। नहीं है, तो method रुक जाता है।
और indefinite integral के लिए, आखिर में हमेशा वापस x में बदलो, answer कभी u में मत छोड़ो।

board_events.text: The two patterns and four results to know
In words: a numerator that is the derivative of the denominator integrates to log of the denominator.

board_events.latex: \int \tan x\,dx = \ln|\sec x| + C \qquad \int \cot x\,dx = \ln|\sin x| + C
\int \sec x\,dx = \ln|\sec x + \tan x| + C \qquad \int \csc x\,dx = \ln|\csc x - \cot x| + C

board_events.text: The $\tan$ and $\sec$ results are the $\int f'/f$ pattern in disguise — numerator equals the denominator's derivative.
Reflex: is the numerator a constant times the derivative of the denominator? If yes, the answer is a log.

segments.text: Substitution has two master patterns; memorise these and half of exam integrals fall instantly.
First, the logarithmic pattern: the integral of f prime over f is log of the absolute value of f.
Say it in words, whenever the numerator is exactly the derivative of the denominator, the answer is log of that denominator. This one reflex is worth a lot of marks.
Second, the power-chain pattern: a function to the n, times its own derivative, integrates like the power rule, f to the n plus one, over n plus one.
From these we derive four standard results. Tan x integrates to log mod sec x; cot x to log mod sin x.
And the trickier pair: sec x integrates to log mod sec x plus tan x; cosec x to log mod cosec x minus cot x.
Both the tan and sec results are secretly the f prime over f pattern, in each case the numerator turns out to be the derivative of the denominator.
So train one question before you compute: is the numerator a constant times the derivative of the denominator? If yes, write log immediately, no formal substitution needed.
Substitution के दो master patterns हैं; इन्हें रट लो तो आधे exam integrals तुरंत गिर जाते हैं।
पहला, logarithmic pattern: integral of f prime over f होता है log of the absolute value of f।
शब्दों में, जब भी numerator ठीक denominator का derivative हो, answer उस denominator का log है। यह एक reflex बहुत marks दिलाता है।
दूसरा, power-chain pattern: कोई function to the n, times उसका अपना derivative, power rule की तरह integrate होता है, f to the n plus one, बटा n plus one।
इनसे चार standard results निकलते हैं। Tan x integrate होकर log mod sec x; cot x होकर log mod sin x।
और मुश्किल जोड़ी: sec x integrate होकर log mod sec x plus tan x; cosec x होकर log mod cosec x minus cot x।
Tan और sec दोनों results असल में f prime over f pattern ही हैं, हर बार numerator निकलता है denominator का derivative।
तो compute से पहले एक सवाल की आदत डालो: क्या numerator, denominator के derivative का constant multiple है? हाँ, तो सीधे log लिखो, औपचारिक substitution की ज़रूरत नहीं।

sections.title: Substitution examples: spot the inner function

board_events.text: Example 1: the derivative is already there
Evaluate $\int 2x\sqrt{x^2+1}\,dx$. Let $u=x^2+1$, so $du=2x\,dx$.
Example 2: spot f-prime over f instantly
Evaluate $\int \frac{x}{x^2+4}\,dx$. Derivative of $x^2+4$ is $2x$, and $x=\tfrac{1}{2}(2x)$.
Numerator a constant times the denominator's derivative? Write (constant) times ln(denominator) at once.

segments.text: Let's spot inner functions in the wild. First, one where the derivative is handed to us.
We want the integral of two x times root x squared plus one. Let u be x squared plus one; then d u is exactly two x d x, and that two x d x is sitting right there.
So the integral becomes root u d u, which is u to the three-halves, over three-halves, that is, two-thirds u to the three-halves.
Back-substitute u equals x squared plus one, and we're done: two-thirds times x squared plus one, to the three-halves, plus C.
<excited>Now watch how the f prime over f reflex skips the busywork entirely.
We want the integral of x over x squared plus four. The derivative of the denominator is two x, and our numerator x is just half of that.
So pull out the one-half: the integral becomes one-half log of x squared plus four, plus C, no formal u needed.
That's the shortcut: whenever the numerator is a constant times the denominator's derivative, write constant times log of the denominator immediately.
आओ inner functions पहचानें। पहले वो, जहाँ derivative पहले से हाथ में है।
हमें integral चाहिए two x times root x square plus one का। मान लो u है x square plus one; तो d u ठीक two x d x, और वो two x d x वहीं मौजूद है।
तो integral बन जाता है root u d u, यानी u to the three-halves, बटा three-halves, मतलब two-thirds u to the three-halves।
वापस रखो u बराबर x square plus one, और हो गया: two-thirds times x square plus one, to the three-halves, plus C।
<excited>अब देखो f prime over f reflex कैसे पूरी मेहनत छोड़ देता है।
हमें integral चाहिए x बटा x square plus four का। Denominator का derivative है two x, और हमारा numerator x उसका बस आधा है।
तो one-half बाहर निकालो: integral बन जाता है one-half log of x square plus four, plus C, कोई औपचारिक u नहीं चाहिए।
यही shortcut है: जब भी numerator, denominator के derivative का constant multiple हो, तुरंत constant times log of denominator लिख दो।

board_events.text: Example 3: a nested substitution
Evaluate $\int \frac{e^{\sqrt{x}}}{\sqrt{x}}\,dx$. Let $u=\sqrt{x}$, so $\frac{dx}{\sqrt{x}}=2\,du$.
Example 4: substitute the root away
Evaluate $\int \frac{1}{1+\sqrt{x}}\,dx$. Put $x=t^2$ ($t\ge 0$): $dx=2t\,dt$, $\sqrt{x}=t$.
The split $\frac{t}{1+t}=1-\frac{1}{1+t}$ (an improper fraction) is a recurring trick — keep it handy.

segments.text: This one nests a root inside an exponent, perfect for a clean substitution.
We want the integral of e to the root x, over root x. Let u be root x; then d u is one over two root x d x, which means d x over root x equals two d u.
Rewrite the integral: e to the root x times d x over root x becomes e to the u times two d u, which is just two e to the u, plus C.
Back-substitute u equals root x: the answer is two e to the root x, plus C. The awkward one over root x was exactly twice the derivative of the exponent.
<curious>Now what if the root blocks every table entry? Substitute it away entirely.
We want the integral of one over one plus root x. Put x equals t squared, so d x is two t d t and root x is just t.
The integral becomes two t over one plus t d t. Split that improper fraction as one minus one over one plus t, and integrate: two times t minus log mod one plus t.
Back-substitute t equals root x: two root x minus two log of one plus root x, plus C.
Tuck away that move, splitting t over one plus t into one minus one over one plus t. That improper-fraction split shows up again and again.
यह एक root को exponent के अंदर nest करता है, एक साफ़ substitution के लिए perfect।
हमें integral चाहिए e to the root x, बटा root x का। मान लो u है root x; तो d u है one over two root x d x, यानी d x बटा root x बराबर two d u।
Integral फिर से लिखो: e to the root x times d x over root x बन जाता है e to the u times two d u, यानी बस two e to the u, plus C।
वापस रखो u बराबर root x: answer है two e to the root x, plus C। वो अटपटा one over root x ठीक exponent के derivative का दुगुना था।
<curious>अब क्या हो जब root हर table entry को रोक दे? उसे पूरी तरह substitute करके हटा दो।
हमें integral चाहिए one over one plus root x का। रखो x बराबर t square, तो d x है two t d t और root x बस t है।
Integral बन जाता है two t बटा one plus t d t. उस improper fraction को one minus one over one plus t की तरह split करो, और integrate करो: two times t minus log mod one plus t।
वापस रखो t बराबर root x: two root x minus two log of one plus root x, plus C।
यह move याद रखो, t over one plus t को one minus one over one plus t में तोड़ना। यह improper-fraction split बार-बार आता है।

board_events.text: Where substitution quietly goes wrong
Replace $g'(x)\,dx$ with $du$ — not just $g(x)$ with $u$. Dropping the $du$ is the number-one error.
For an indefinite integral, always back-substitute to $x$. Leaving the answer in $u$ loses marks.
Mind the constant factor in $f'/f$: $\int\frac{x}{x^2+a^2}$ carries a $\tfrac{1}{2}$; $\int\frac{2x}{x^2+a^2}$ does not.
Sign check: $\int\tan x = +\ln|\sec x|$ and $\int\cot x = +\ln|\sin x|$.
Substitution only works if $g'$ is present. If it isn't, don't force it — reach for a different method.
The reflex handling a huge share of exam integrals: check if the numerator is the derivative of the denominator first.

segments.text: A few small habits separate a clean substitution from a wrong one. Let's name them.
First and biggest: you must replace g prime of x d x with d u, not just swap g of x for u. Dropping the d u accounting is the single most common substitution error.
Second: for an indefinite integral, always convert back to x. An answer left in u is incomplete and loses marks.

Third, the constant factor. The integral of x over x squared plus a squared carries a one-half; but two x over x squared plus a squared does not. Check whether your numerator is the whole derivative or a fraction of it.
Fourth, a sign check: tan x integrates to plus log mod sec x, and cot x to plus log mod sin x. Get the signs from the derivation, not from guessing.
And remember, substitution only works if g prime is actually present. If it isn't, don't force the method, step back and pick another.
The board sums up the golden reflex: if the numerator is a constant times the derivative of the denominator, the answer is a log.
<whisper>Ask that one question before you write anything, and a huge share of exam integrals become one-liners.
कुछ छोटी आदतें एक साफ़ substitution को गलत से अलग करती हैं। चलो इन्हें नाम दें।
पहली और सबसे बड़ी: g prime of x d x को d u से बदलना ज़रूरी है, सिर्फ़ g of x को u से नहीं। d u की accounting छोड़ना सबसे common substitution error है।
दूसरी: indefinite integral के लिए हमेशा वापस x में बदलो। u में छोड़ा answer अधूरा है और marks खोता है।
तीसरी, constant factor। Integral of x over x square plus a square में one-half आता है; पर two x over x square plus a square में नहीं। देखो numerator पूरा derivative है या उसका अंश।
चौथी, sign check: tan x integrate होकर plus log mod sec x, और cot x होकर plus log mod sin x. Signs derivation से लो, अंदाज़े से नहीं।
और याद रखो, substitution तभी चलता है जब g prime मौजूद हो। नहीं है, तो method को ज़बरदस्ती मत थोपो, पीछे हटकर दूसरा चुनो।
Board golden reflex बताता है: अगर numerator, denominator के derivative का constant multiple है, तो answer एक log है।
<whisper>कुछ भी लिखने से पहले वही एक सवाल पूछो, और exam के बहुत सारे integrals one-liner बन जाएँगे।

board_events.text: First rewrite, then integrate
You can't integrate $\sin^2 x$ directly — there's no table entry for it.
Identities convert powers and products of sines and cosines into sums of plain $\sin(kx)$ and $\cos(kx)$.

board_events.text: Each plain $\sin(kx)$ or $\cos(kx)$ integrates instantly, so the whole thing becomes term-by-term.
Walli's formula applies only to definite integrals over $[0,\tfrac{\pi}{2}]$ — never indefinite ones.
The method is a two-step dance: pick the right identity for the shape, then integrate each term.

segments.text: Here's a whole class of integrals the table can't touch on its own, and one idea that cracks all of them.
Try to integrate sine squared x. There's simply no table entry for it, so a direct attack fails.
The fix is identities. They convert awkward powers and products of sines and cosines into sums of plain sine k x and cosine k x, each of which we can integrate on sight.
The two workhorses are the power-reduction formulas: sine squared x is one minus cosine two x, all over two; cosine squared x is one plus cosine two x, over two.
Think of a musical chord, it sounds complex, but it's just pure tones stacked together. Identities are the spectrum analyser that breaks a trig chord into those pure tones.
<excited>And every pure tone is trivial to integrate, so the whole problem collapses into term-by-term integration.
One boundary to respect: Walli's formula, which we'll use for high powers, works only for definite integrals from zero to pi over two, never for indefinite ones.
So the method is really a two-step dance: first pick the identity that matches the shape, then integrate each resulting term.
यह integrals का एक पूरा वर्ग है जिसे table अकेले नहीं छू सकता, और एक idea जो इन सबको तोड़ देता है।
Sine square x को integrate करने की कोशिश करो। इसकी कोई table entry है ही नहीं, तो सीधा हमला fail हो जाता है।
इलाज है identities। ये sines और cosines के अटपटे powers और products को plain sine k x और cosine k x के sums में बदल देती हैं, जिनमें से हर एक देखते ही integrate हो जाता है।
दो workhorses हैं power-reduction formulas: sine square x है one minus cosine two x, बटा two; cosine square x है one plus cosine two x, बटा two।
एक musical chord सोचो, सुनने में complex, पर असल में बस pure tones एक साथ। Identities वो spectrum analyser हैं जो trig chord को उन pure tones में तोड़ती हैं।
<excited>और हर pure tone integrate करना trivial है, तो पूरी problem term-by-term integration में सिमट जाती है।
एक सीमा का ध्यान: Walli's formula, जो हम high powers के लिए इस्तेमाल करेंगे, सिर्फ़ zero to pi over two के definite integrals के लिए है, indefinite के लिए कभी नहीं।
तो method असल में दो-step का नाच है: पहले shape से match करती identity चुनो, फिर हर term को integrate करो।

board_events.text: Identities that make trig integrable
Choose by shape: even power uses power-reduction; odd power peels one factor and substitutes; a product uses product-to-sum.
Powers of $\tan/\sec$: use $\sec^2 x = 1+\tan^2 x$ and peel off a $\sec^2 x$ to substitute.

segments.text: This is the dictionary. Every trig integral in this subtopic is a lookup into one of these identities.
Power-reduction for even powers: sine squared is one minus cosine two x over two; cosine squared is one plus cosine two x over two. Note the sign difference, that trips people up.
Triple-angle forms handle cubes: sine cubed is three sine x minus sine three x, over four; cosine cubed is three cosine x plus cosine three x, over four.
For a sine-times-cosine product, use two sine A cosine B equals sine of A plus B plus sine of A minus B.
The companion product-to-sum identities: two cosine A cosine B, and two sine A sine B, each collapse to a sum or difference of cosines.
The strategy is to classify by shape. Even power? Power-reduction. Odd power? Peel one factor off and substitute. A product? Product-to-sum.
For definite integrals from zero to pi over two of sine to the n cosine to the m, Walli's formula gives the answer as a ratio of double-factorials, with a pi-over-two only when both powers are even.
And for powers of tan or sec, use secant squared equals one plus tan squared, then peel off a secant squared to substitute.
यह रही dictionary। इस subtopic का हर trig integral इन्हीं identities में से किसी का lookup है।
Even powers के लिए power-reduction: sine square है one minus cosine two x बटा two; cosine square है one plus cosine two x बटा two। Sign का फ़र्क़ ध्यान से, यही लोगों को फँसाता है।
Cubes को triple-angle forms सँभालते हैं: sine cube है three sine x minus sine three x, बटा four; cosine cube है three cosine x plus cosine three x, बटा four।
Sine-times-cosine product के लिए, इस्तेमाल करो two sine A cosine B बराबर sine of A plus B plus sine of A minus B।
साथी product-to-sum identities: two cosine A cosine B, और two sine A sine B, हर एक cosines के sum या difference में सिमट जाती है।
Strategy है shape से classify करना। Even power? Power-reduction. Odd power? एक factor छीलो और substitute करो। Product? Product-to-sum।

Zero to pi over two के definite integrals में sine to the n cosine to the m के लिए, Walli's formula answer देता है double-factorials के ratio के रूप में, pi-over-two सिर्फ़ तभी जब दोनों powers even हों।
और tan या sec के powers के लिए, secant square बराबर one plus tan square इस्तेमाल करो, फिर एक secant square छीलकर substitute करो।

board_events.text: Example 1: an even power
Evaluate $\int \cos^2 x\,dx$. Use $\cos^2 x = \frac{1+\cos 2x}{2}$.
Example 2: a product of two frequencies
Evaluate $\int \sin 5x\cos 3x\,dx$. Product-to-sum: $2\sin 5x\cos 3x = \sin 8x + \sin 2x$.
Never try parts on a sine-cosine product — product-to-sum makes it two trivial integrals.

segments.text: Let's run the two most common trig moves. First, an even power.
We want the integral of cosine squared x. There's no direct entry, so use power-reduction: cosine squared is one plus cosine two x, over two.

Now each piece is trivial. One-half integrates to x over two; cosine two x integrates to sine two x over two, then halved again, giving sine two x over four. So the answer is x over two plus sine two x over four, plus C.
<curious>Next, a product of two different frequencies, where a smart identity beats brute force.
We want the integral of sine five x cosine three x. Product-to-sum says two sine five x cosine three x equals sine eight x plus sine two x.
So the integral is one-half times the integral of sine eight x plus sine two x.
Integrating each sine gives minus cosine over its frequency; after the one-half, we get minus cosine eight x over sixteen, minus cosine two x over four, plus C.
The lesson: never reach for integration by parts on a sine-cosine product. Product-to-sum turns it into two trivial integrals.
चलो दो सबसे common trig moves चलाएँ। पहले, एक even power।
हमें integral चाहिए cosine square x का। कोई direct entry नहीं, तो power-reduction इस्तेमाल करो: cosine square है one plus cosine two x, बटा two।
अब हर piece trivial है। One-half integrate होकर x बटा two; cosine two x integrate होकर sine two x बटा two, फिर आधा, यानी sine two x बटा four। तो answer है x बटा two plus sine two x बटा four, plus C।
<curious>अगला, दो अलग frequencies का product, जहाँ एक चतुर identity brute force को हरा देती है।
हमें integral चाहिए sine five x cosine three x का। Product-to-sum कहता है two sine five x cosine three x बराबर sine eight x plus sine two x।
तो integral है one-half times integral of sine eight x plus sine two x।
हर sine integrate होकर minus cosine बटा उसकी frequency; one-half के बाद मिलता है minus cosine eight x बटा sixteen, minus cosine two x बटा four, plus C।
सबक: sine-cosine product पर integration by parts कभी मत उठाओ। Product-to-sum इसे दो trivial integrals बना देता है।

sections.title: Trig examples: odd powers and Walli's formula

board_events.text: Example 3: an odd power, peel and substitute
Evaluate $\int \sin^3 x\cos^2 x\,dx$. Peel one $\sin x$: $\sin^3 x = (1-\cos^2 x)\sin x$.
Let $u=\cos x$, $du=-\sin x\,dx$.
Example 4: Walli's formula
Evaluate $\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\sin^6 x\cos^2 x\,dx$. Here $n=6$, $m=2$, both even, so the $\tfrac{\pi}{2}$ branch applies.
Walli collapses a brutal expansion into one double-factorial fraction — priceless when time is short.

segments.text: Odd powers get a different treatment, peel and substitute.
We want the integral of sine cubed x cosine squared x. Since the sine power is odd, peel off one sine x and convert the rest: sine cubed becomes one minus cosine squared, times sine x.
Now let u be cosine x, so d u is minus sine x d x, and that spare sine x is exactly what we need.
The integral becomes minus the integral of one minus u squared, times u squared, d u, that is minus u cubed over three, minus u to the fifth over five, with the sign worked through.
Back-substitute u equals cosine x, and after tidying signs the answer is cosine to the fifth x over five, minus cosine cubed x over three, plus C.
<excited>Now a definite integral where Walli's formula turns a nightmare into one line.
We want the integral from zero to pi over two of sine to the sixth x, cosine squared x. Here n is six and m is two, both even, so the pi-over-two branch of Walli applies.

Plug in the double-factorials: five double-factorial times one double-factorial, over eight double-factorial, times pi over two. That's fifteen over three hundred eighty-four, times pi over two, which simplifies to five pi over two hundred fifty-six.
See what Walli bought us: it collapsed a brutal expansion into a single double-factorial fraction. When the clock is running, that's priceless.
Odd powers का इलाज अलग है, peel करो और substitute करो।
हमें integral चाहिए sine cube x cosine square x का। चूँकि sine की power odd है, एक sine x छीलो और बाकी को बदलो: sine cube बनता है one minus cosine square, times sine x।
अब मान लो u है cosine x, तो d u है minus sine x d x, और वो बचा हुआ sine x ठीक वही है जो चाहिए।
Integral बन जाता है minus integral of one minus u square, times u square, d u, यानी minus u cube बटा three, minus u to the fifth बटा five, sign सँभालते हुए।
वापस रखो u बराबर cosine x, और signs ठीक करने पर answer है cosine to the fifth x बटा five, minus cosine cube x बटा three, plus C।
<excited>अब एक definite integral जहाँ Walli's formula एक nightmare को एक line बना देता है।
हमें integral चाहिए zero to pi over two, sine to the sixth x, cosine square x का। यहाँ n है six और m है two, दोनों even, तो Walli का pi-over-two branch लगता है।

Double-factorials रखो: five double-factorial times one double-factorial, बटा eight double-factorial, times pi over two। यह है fifteen बटा three hundred eighty-four, times pi over two, जो सिमटकर बनता है five pi बटा two hundred fifty-six।
देखो Walli ने क्या दिया: एक brutal expansion को एक अकेले double-factorial fraction में सिकोड़ दिया। जब घड़ी चल रही हो, यह अनमोल है।

board_events.text: Trig traps to sidestep
$\int \sin^2 x\,dx \neq \frac{\sin^3 x}{3}$. The power rule integrates powers of $x$, not of $\sin x$ — use an identity first.
Don't try parts on $\sin(ax)\cos(bx)$ — product-to-sum is faster and avoids circular parts.
Watch the double-angle sign: $\sin^2 x$ uses $1-\cos 2x$; $\cos^2 x$ uses $1+\cos 2x$.
Walli's formula is only for $\int_0^{\pi/2}$. Never use it on an indefinite integral or with other limits.
Classify by shape: even power halve it; odd power peel one off and substitute; product product-to-sum.
Naming the shape picks the identity automatically — most of the work is recognition, not algebra.

segments.text: Trig integrals have a handful of signature traps. Name them once and you'll stop falling in.
The big one: the integral of sine squared x is not sine cubed over three. The power rule integrates powers of x, not powers of sine x, you must apply an identity first.
Next: don't reach for integration by parts on a sine times cosine product. Product-to-sum is faster and skips the circular parts loop entirely.
Watch the double-angle sign carefully. Sine squared uses one minus cosine two x; cosine squared uses one plus cosine two x. Mixing them flips a sign and wrecks the answer.
And Walli's formula is strictly for the definite integral from zero to pi over two. Never apply it to an indefinite integral, or with any other limits.
The habit that prevents all of these: classify by shape before you compute. Even power, halve it; odd power, peel one off and substitute; product, product-to-sum.
The board says it in one line, even, odd, and product each map to a fixed move.
<whisper>Name the shape and the identity picks itself. Most of the battle here is recognition, not algebra.
Trig integrals के कुछ signature traps हैं। एक बार नाम दे दो, फिर गिरना बंद।
सबसे बड़ा: sine square x का integral, sine cube बटा three नहीं है। Power rule x के powers को integrate करता है, sine x के powers को नहीं, पहले identity लगाना ज़रूरी है।
अगला: sine times cosine product पर integration by parts मत उठाओ। Product-to-sum तेज़ है और circular parts का चक्कर पूरी तरह छोड़ देता है।
Double-angle sign को ध्यान से देखो। Sine square में one minus cosine two x; cosine square में one plus cosine two x। इन्हें मिलाया तो sign पलटेगा और answer बिगड़ेगा।
और Walli's formula सख़्ती से zero to pi over two के definite integral के लिए है। इसे indefinite integral पर, या किसी और limits के साथ कभी मत लगाओ।
वो आदत जो इन सबको रोकती है: compute से पहले shape से classify करो। Even power, आधा करो; odd power, एक छीलो और substitute करो; product, product-to-sum।
Board इसे एक line में कहता है, even, odd, और product हर एक एक तय move पर जाता है।
<whisper>Shape को नाम दो और identity खुद चुन जाती है। यहाँ ज़्यादातर लड़ाई recognition की है, algebra की नहीं।
